disposition: The complete 16-row Time/Gravity campaign is internally consistent and all frozen source/archive preservation checks pass. Thirteen rows pass. Direct Time docked/floated and worker Gravity floated fail the unchanged callback p95 limit. Two prior Time/Gravity callback failures clear in this follow-up, while the historical v2 and Wave records remain intact. The candidate is not performance-release approved.

method.execution: Read-only source/manifest/ZIP checks and independent reconstruction of existing raw reports. No tests, browser, builds, GPU or numerical campaign was launched.
method.statistics: Nearest-rank ceil(n*q)-1 with clipping; ascending sort followed by sequential binary64 accumulation and division reproduces the declared probe algorithm. Every summary field matches exactly without a tolerance.
method.scope: All frame and callback vectors, including every diagnostic ownerRead series, and all action durations were reconstructed. Only standalone method:ownerRead.* diagnostics are excluded from the interface callback gate as preregistered. Nested owner reads remain inside inclusive callback timings; nested durations are not added as independent wall time.

baseline_comparison.boundary: These are descriptive matches by panel, scenario, backend size and visibility with unchanged gates and renderer class. V2 retained only frame/callback aggregates, so its raw distributions cannot be reconstructed. Owner tick intervals, initial histories and scheduling differ across runs. The comparison does not isolate a causal effect of any implementation change, establish statistical significance, or certify common sample time.
baseline_comparison.historical_disposition: The sealed v2 campaign remains 279/288 rows passing with nine callback failures. The five Time/Gravity failures in that record are retained; this follow-up records two corresponding rows now passing and three still failing. Wave v3's four visible callback failures and other panel failures remain separate unremeasured work.

predecessor_preservation.historical_attachment_limit: V2 raw reports and failure log remain preserved. Its transient panel screenshots/error-context were cleared by a later invocation and are not retroactively supplied by the newer Wave or Time/Gravity attachments.

limitations: This is independent reconstruction of retained measurements, not a second browser campaign or universal 60 FPS guarantee.

Raw frame intervals and callback durations are retained, but their absolute timing origins and callback start/stop timestamps are not. The reported measurement duration cannot be independently reconstructed from these vectors.
The existing stop protocol may collect installed callbacks during its zero-delay drain after stoppedAt. Retained vectors and summary calculations cover that same collected data.
Actions measure dispatch to next foreground requestAnimationFrame, not physical display presentation.

Same-owner/generation/readiness flags and endpoint clock checks satisfy the registered lifecycle contract. They do not prove that J/E, slab data, telemetry and other observations share a microscopic tick or state identity.
Direct lifecycle records are null; worker lifecycle fields are checked where present. Zero endpoint resource deltas over these windows do not prove absence of all leaks or races.
Canvas and DOM counters measure selected operations under the tested panel root; they do not establish complete histories, scientific sample cadence, numerical equality or observation provenance.
Hardware renderer, no Long Tasks and no runtime errors apply only to these windows and instrumentation.
No strict-law adoption, continuum or matter recovery, spectra, chemistry, causal gravitational recovery, commit, public deployment or release approval follows.
